subject: literature
passage: For nine years, Mr. Haddad had come into the tailor's shop on the first Monday of every month, always for something small: a button, a hem, a frayed cuff. Yusuf, the tailor, had long suspected that the jackets did not really need mending, but he had never said so. Then one month Mr. Haddad did not come, nor the next. In the third month Yusuf found himself walking, without having decided to, toward the old man's street, a spool of thread in his pocket as if it were a reason.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To reveal that a routine the tailor took for granted had come to matter to him
choices.B: To describe the techniques Yusuf uses to mend clothing
choices.C: To show that Yusuf is annoyed by customers who waste his time
choices.D: To explain why Mr. Haddad's jackets needed so many repairs

explanation.why: The text establishes a long routine of visits that Yusuf suspects are unnecessary and quietly accepts. When the visits stop, Yusuf finds himself going to look for the old man "without having decided to." The passage reveals, through his unplanned walk, that the routine meant more to him than he realized.
explanation.A: Correct. Only when the monthly visits stop does Yusuf discover, by walking to the old man's street, how much they mattered to him.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text names small jobs like buttons and hems but describes no tailoring techniques.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Yusuf never complains about the visits and goes looking for Mr. Haddad when they stop, which shows concern, not annoyance.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Yusuf suspects the jackets "did not really need mending"; the text never explains any repairs.
